1.title: CVE-2026-129453 (CVSS 9.9)
1.summary: A vulnerability was found in DrayTek Vigor2960 1.5.1.6. This issue affects the function check_file_exist of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi of the component File Existence Check. Performing a manipulation of the argument upload_name results in heap-based buffer overflow. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is capable of addressing this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

1.title: CVE-2026-129483 (CVSS 9.1)
1.summary: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared secret, authenticating as any existing user without the password and learning session keys.

1.title: CVE-2026-129550 (CVSS 9.1)
1.summary: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in @tensei/auth that allows unauthenticated or authenticated users to assign themselves arbitrary roles via the exposed User Roles field. Attackers can supply a roles array during registration, a POST to the users route, or a PATCH to their own record to gain administrator permissions.

1.title: CVE-2026-129552 (CVSS 9.8)
1.summary: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in @tensei/auth that falls back to the hard-coded JWT signing key 'auth-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset. Unauthenticated attackers can sign tokens with arbitrary user ids accepted by populateContextFromToken to impersonate any user, including administrators.

1.title: CVE-2026-129941 (CVSS 9.8)
1.summary: Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register accounts via the createUser mutation on /prime/graphql. Because the isAuthenticated() guard has its check commented out and createAbility() hard-codes every role to admin, attackers can log in with full administrative control over content, users, webhooks and settings.

1.title: CVE-2026-129952 (CVSS 9.8)
1.summary: NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain administrator access by forging JWTs with the hardcoded 'nodepress-secret' fallback key. Attackers can sign HS256 bearer tokens with the default issuer, audience, and role 'admin' to access administrator-only APIs for article, comment, options, and file management.

1.title: CVE-2026-129955 (CVSS 9.8)
1.summary: NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator access by using the hardcoded default password 'root'. Attackers can send base64-encoded 'root' to POST /admin/login when NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD is unset to obtain admin tokens and fully control the site.

1.title: GHSA-m9j8-jcmv-hp69 — SvelteKit: Build-time server-only module import guard could fail, resulting in server secrets being statically replaced in client bundle
1.summary: Under certain circumstances, server-only imports, which typically cannot be included in the client bundle, could make their way into it, potentially exposing secrets. This could only occur when those server-only imports were made through `src/params.js`.

1.title: GHSA-3r8g-jcqq-3p5j — SvelteKit: DoS while parsing form data from a remote functions `form`
1.summary: This only affects applications using the experimental remote functions flag and utilizing the `form`, `query`, or `command` remote functions. A specially-crafted request could block the event loop for extended periods of time during parsing.

1.title: GHSA-jm3w-gw2p-xjfj — AIOHTTP: Event loop stall in add_domain() wildcard matching
1.summary:
### Summary

`Application.add_domain()` compiled each `*` in a host mask to `[^:]*`. With two or more wildcards in a mask, matching a long `Host` header that does not match the mask took polynomial time on the event loop.

### Impact

An attacker could stall a server that registers a domain mask with more than one wildcard by sending requests with a long `Host` header.

### Workaround

Use at most one `*` in a domain mask.

---

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/c6ac0e44c3c573ff9616f4a6a532992538b31e43

1.title: GHSA-xgw8-8ccx-rmqh — AIOHTTP: Too many URL-encoded form fields block the event loop
1.summary:
### Summary

`Request.post()` had no limit on the number of fields in a URL-encoded form body. Inserting a large number of repeated keys into a `MultiDict` took quadratic time on the event loop.

### Impact

An attacker could block the event loop with a form POST within the default `client_max_size` to any handler that calls `Request.post()`.

---

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/615fec3d4f088f30d2ee72cad760152e92aa1c53

1.title: GHSA-24c4-3p7v-29cm — AIOHTTP: Base64 multipart parts bypass client_max_size
1.summary:
### Summary

When reading a multipart part with `Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`, `BodyPartReader.read_chunk()` kept reading until the chunk length was a multiple of 4, with no byte limit. A part with a short `Content-Length`, or a long run of whitespace, could cause the entire remaining body to be read into memory within a single call before any size check, or spin on the event loop.

### Impact

An attacker could bypass `client_max_size` to cause excessive memory use, or block the event loop, with a specially crafted multipart request to any handler that reads multipart data.

1.title: GHSA-3rp8-rxj8-mvjw — AIOHTTP: WebSocket max_msg_size bypass via integer overflow
1.summary:
### Summary

The `max_msg_size` check in the WebSocket reader added the declared frame length to the size of the partial message already buffered. In the C extension this addition is 64-bit arithmetic, so a declared length close to 2**63 overflowed and the check passed.

### Impact

An attacker could bypass `max_msg_size` and cause unbounded memory use by streaming an oversized WebSocket message after a small non-final fragment.

### Workaround

If unable to upgrade, the Python reader is unaffected and can be used with `AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1`.

---

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp

1.title: GHSA-pw86-h8fm-j323 — AIOHTTP: Unbounded buffering of data received during an upgrade request
1.summary:
### Summary

While a request flagged as an upgrade (e.g. a WebSocket handshake) was being handled, all further data received on the connection was buffered with no size limit or flow control until the handler completed.

### Impact

An attacker could cause unbounded memory use by streaming data behind an upgrade request to any handler that does not immediately accept or reject the upgrade.

---

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/3d850ee9b92573c7e913821cbcb96005beb3f4df

1.title: GHSA-28qf-cpwq-vmc2 — AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade
1.summary:
### Summary

When the pipelined request queue was full, the pure-Python parser stored the unparsed remainder internally and also returned it to the caller. After a handler declined an upgrade request, the buffered data was re-fed, so the buffer grew with each handled request and already-handled requests were dispatched to the application again.

1.title: GHSA-h4cc-hm5h-fmm9 — AIOHTTP: Concatenated compressed streams cause excessive CPU use
1.summary:
### Summary

When decompressing a payload made up of many concatenated compressed members (gzip, deflate or zstd), each member was decoded by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, resulting in quadratic CPU time. Empty members produce no output, so `client_max_size` and output backpressure did not limit the work.

### Impact

An attacker could block the event loop of a server with a specially crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message. A malicious server could do the same to a client.

---

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/d925a80539ffd227da1d93ab

1.title: GHSA-5rmc-48h2-hvcm — AIOHTTP: WebSocket receive queue limits bypassed by small or compressed messages
1.summary:
### Summary

The WebSocket reader continued parsing frames already received after the receive queue had paused the transport, and empty messages were not counted towards the queue size. With permessage-deflate, a single read of compressed frames could add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the queue.

### Impact

An attacker could cause excessive memory use in a WebSocket server, or a malicious server against a client, by sending many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them.

---

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0ae507423f681161efa77d200
